A slip-based blending law divides the braking demand between the motor and the friction brakes. In simulation over a 12 km urban cycle the controller recovers 14.8 per cent of the traction energy and raises the range from 62 to 71 km, with no loss of stopping distance below 8 m from 30 km/h.</w:t></w:r></w:p><w:p><w:r><w:rPr><w:rFonts w:ascii="Courier New" w:hAnsi="Courier New"/></w:rPr><w:t>\tableofcontents</w:t></w:r></w:p><w:p><w:pPr><w:pStyle w:val="Heading1"/></w:pPr><w:r><w:t xml:space="preserve">1 </w:t></w:r><w:r><w:t>Introduction</w:t></w:r></w:p><w:p><w:pPr><w:jc w:val="both"/></w:pPr><w:r><w:t xml:space="preserve">Light electric vehicles spend most of their energy accelerating a small mass repeatedly, so the share that can be recovered when braking is large </w:t></w:r><w:r><w:t>[1, 2]</w:t></w:r><w:r><w:t>. The difficulty is that the motor can brake only within the limits of its torque and of the battery's charge acceptance, while the driver expects the same pedal feel as with friction brakes.</w:t></w:r></w:p><w:p><w:pPr><w:jc w:val="both"/></w:pPr><w:r><w:t>The objective is a controller that maximizes the recovered energy subject to three constraints: the battery current limit, Sokolov</w:t></w:r></w:p><w:p><w:r><w:rPr><w:i/></w:rPr><w:t>The thesis studies the estimation of the power spectrum from records of fewer than 100 samples. A regularized autoregressive estimator is proposed and shown to reduce the mean squared error of the peak frequency by 31 per cent against the periodogram on synthetic signals.</w:t></w:r></w:p><w:p><w:r><w:rPr><w:rFonts w:ascii="Courier New" w:hAnsi="Courier New"/></w:rPr><w:t>\tableofcontents</w:t></w:r></w:p><w:p><w:pPr><w:pStyle w:val="Heading1"/></w:pPr><w:r><w:t xml:space="preserve">1 </w:t></w:r><w:r><w:t>Introduction</w:t></w:r></w:p><w:p><w:pPr><w:jc w:val="both"/></w:pPr><w:r><w:t xml:space="preserve">Many measured signals are short: a clinical recording, a single seasonal cycle, a transient in a power line. The most probable cause is the temperature of the air inside the tube, which is cooled by the water column and may be a degree or so below the room temperature (</w:t></w:r><m:oMath><m:r><m:t>Δv≈0.6</m:t></m:r></m:oMath><w:r><w:t xml:space="preserve"> m/s per kelvin). Repeating this produces nested closed intervals whose lengths tend to zero, so they share a single point </w:t></w:r><m:oMath><m:r><m:t>ℓ</m:t></m:r></m:oMath><w:r><w:t xml:space="preserve">, and the chosen terms converge to </w:t></w:r><m:oMath><m:r><m:t>ℓ</m:t></m:r></m:oMath><w:r><w:t>.</w:t></w:r></w:p><w:p><w:r><w:t xml:space="preserve">For </w:t></w:r><m:oMath><m:sSup><m:e><m:r><m:rPr><m:scr m:val="double-struck"/></m:rPr><m:t>R</m:t></m:r></m:e><m:sup><m:r><m:t>n</m:t></m:r></m:sup></m:sSup></m:oMath><w:r><w:t xml:space="preserve"> apply the one-dimensional argument to the coordinates one after another, passing to a subsequence each time.</w:t></w:r></w:p><w:p><w:pPr><w:pStyle w:val="Heading2"/></w:pPr><w:r><w:t xml:space="preserve">1.4 </w:t></w:r><w:r><w:t>Compactness and continuity</w:t></w:r></w:p><w:p><w:r><w:rPr><w:b/><w:i w:val="0"/></w:rPr><w:t xml:space="preserve">Proposition. </w:t></w:r><w:r><w:t xml:space="preserve">If </w:t></w:r><m:oMath><m:r><m:t>K</m:t></m:r></m:oMath><w:r><w:t xml:space="preserve"> is compact and </w:t></w:r><m:oMath><m:r><m:t>f:K→Y</m:t></m:r></m:oMath><w:r><w:t xml:space="preserve"> is continuous, then </w:t></w:r><m:oMath><m:r><m:t>f(K)</m:t></m:r></m:oMath><w:r><w:t xml:space="preserve"> is compact.</w:t></w:r></w:p><w:p><w:r><w:rPr><w:b w:val="0"/><w:i/></w:rPr><w:t xml:space="preserve">Proof. </w:t></w:r><w:r><w:t xml:space="preserve">Let </w:t></w:r><m:oMath><m:r><m:t>{</m:t></m:r><m:sSub><m:e><m:r><m:t>V</m:t></m:r></m:e><m:sub><m:r><m:t>α</m:t></m:r></m:sub></m:sSub><m:r><m:t>}</m:t></m:r></m:oMath><w:r><w:t xml:space="preserve"> be an open cover of </w:t></w:r><m:oMath><m:r><m:t>f(K)</m:t></m:r></m:oMath><w:r><w:t xml:space="preserve">. The sets </w:t></w:r><m:oMath><m:sSup><m:e><m:r><m:t>f</m:t></m:r></m:e><m:sup><m:r><m:t>−1</m:t></m:r></m:sup></m:sSup><m:r><m:t>(</m:t></m:r><m:sSub><m:e><m:r><m:t>V</m:t></m:r></m:e><m:sub><m:r><m:t>α</m:t></m:r></m:sub></m:sSub><m:r><m:t>)</m:t></m:r></m:oMath><w:r><w:t xml:space="preserve"> are open and cover </w:t></w:r><m:oMath><m:r><m:t>K</m:t></m:r></m:oMath><w:r><w:t xml:space="preserve">, so finitely many of them do; the corresponding </w:t></w:r><m:oMath><m:sSub><m:e><m:r><m:t>V</m:t></m:r></m:e><m:sub><m:r><m:t>α</m:t></m:r></m:sub></m:sSub></m:oMath><w:r><w:t xml:space="preserve"> cover </w:t></w:r><m:oMath><m:r><m:t>f(K)</m:t></m:r></m:oMath><w:r><w:t>.</w:t></w:r></w:p><w:p><w:r><w:rPr><w:b/><w:i w:val="0"/></w:rPr><w:t xml:space="preserve">Theorem (Extreme value theorem). </w:t></w:r><w:r><w:t xml:space="preserve">Let </w:t></w:r><m:oMath><m:r><m:t>K</m:t></m:r></m:oMath><w:r><w:t xml:space="preserve"> be a non-empty compact set and </w:t></w:r><m:oMath><m:r><m:t>f:K→</m:t></m:r><m:r><m:rPr><m:scr m:val="double-struck"/></m:rPr><m:t>R</m:t></m:r></m:oMath><w:r><w:t xml:space="preserve"> continuous. Surface, B. Vacuum and C. Synchrotron</w:t></w:r></w:p><w:p><w:pPr><w:jc w:val="center"/></w:pPr><w:r><w:rPr><w:i/></w:rPr><w:t>Department of Materials, Example University</w:t></w:r></w:p><w:p><w:r><w:rPr><w:i/></w:rPr><w:t>Anatase TiO₂ films grown by atomic layer deposition were annealed in ultra-high vacuum between 300 and 700 °C and analysed in situ by monochromated Al Kα XPS. Peak fitting of the Ti 2p region with spin–orbit-constrained doublets on a Shirley background resolves a Ti³⁺ component 1.7 eV below Ti⁴⁺, whose fraction of the Ti 2p signal rises from 2.1 % to 14.0 % with annealing temperature. The O 1s spectra show a concurrent growth of a hydroxyl / vacancy-adjacent component at 531.3 eV. An Arrhenius analysis of the Ti³⁺ fraction gives an apparent activation energy of 0.23 ± 0.01 eV for vacancy formation.</w:t></w:r></w:p><w:p><w:r><w:rPr><w:b/></w:rPr><w:t xml:space="preserve">Keywords: </w:t></w:r><w:r><w:t>XPS · TiO₂ · oxygen vacancies · peak fitting · Shirley background</w:t></w:r></w:p><w:p><w:pPr><w:pStyle w:val="Heading1"/></w:pPr><w:r><w:t xml:space="preserve">1 </w:t></w:r><w:r><w:t>Introduction</w:t></w:r></w:p><w:p><w:pPr><w:jc w:val="both"/></w:pPr><w:r><w:t xml:space="preserve">Titanium dioxide is the archetypal photocatalyst, and its activity is governed to a large extent by point defects at the surface </w:t></w:r><w:r><w:t>[1]</w:t></w:r><w:r><w:t xml:space="preserve">. Removal of lattice oxygen leaves two excess electrons that localise on neighbouring Ti sites, producing Ti³⁺ centres with a characteristic chemical shift in the Ti 2p spectrum </w:t></w:r><w:r><w:t>[2]</w:t></w:r><w:r><w:t>. Quantifying that component reliably requires a physically constrained fit; in this work we describe a protocol and apply it to a temperature series.</w:t></w:r></w:p><w:p><w:pPr><w:pStyle w:val="Heading1"/></w:pPr><w:r><w:t xml:space="preserve">2 </w:t></w:r><w:r><w:t>Experimental</w:t></w:r></w:p><w:p><w:pPr><w:pStyle w:val="Heading2"/></w:pPr><w:r><w:t xml:space="preserve">2.1 </w:t></w:r><w:r><w:t>Sample preparation</w:t></w:r></w:p><w:p><w:pPr><w:jc w:val="both"/></w:pPr><w:r><w:t>Films of nominal thickness 30 nm were grown on Si(100) by thermal ALD from TiCl₄ and H₂O at 250 °C (600 cycles at 0.5 Å per cycle) and crystallised to anatase by a 1 h anneal in air at 450 °C, confirmed by Raman spectroscopy (Eg mode at 144 cm⁻¹). Medic, I. Statistician and J. Nurse, on behalf of the MOVE-T2D investigators</w:t></w:r></w:p><w:p><w:pPr><w:jc w:val="center"/></w:pPr><w:r><w:rPr><w:i/></w:rPr><w:t>Department of Primary Care, Example University</w:t></w:r></w:p><w:p><w:r><w:rPr><w:i/></w:rPr><w:t>Background: Structured exercise improves glycaemic control, but effect sizes in routine care are uncertain. Methods: 240 adults with type 2 diabetes (HbA1c 7.0–10.0 %) were randomised 1:1 to supervised exercise or usual care. The primary outcome was change in HbA1c at 12 weeks, analysed by intention to treat. Results: HbA1c fell by 0.62 % with exercise versus 0.11 % with usual care (adjusted difference −0.51 %; 95 % CI −0.70 to −0.32; p < 0.001). Conclusions: Supervised exercise produces a clinically meaningful reduction in HbA1c. Guidelines recommend 150 minutes of moderate activity per week, but adherence outside trials is poor. We tested whether a supervised programme delivered in routine primary care lowers HbA1c.</w:t></w:r></w:p><w:p><w:pPr><w:pStyle w:val="Heading1"/></w:pPr><w:r><w:t xml:space="preserve">2 </w:t></w:r><w:r><w:t>Methods</w:t></w:r></w:p><w:p><w:pPr><w:pStyle w:val="Heading2"/></w:pPr><w:r><w:t xml:space="preserve">2.1 </w:t></w:r><w:r><w:t>Design and participants</w:t></w:r></w:p><w:p><w:pPr><w:jc w:val="both"/></w:pPr><w:r><w:t xml:space="preserve">Parallel-group, assessor-blinded randomised trial at four centres, reported according to the CONSORT 2010 statement </w:t></w:r><w:r><w:t>[2]</w:t></w:r><w:r><w:t>. Randomisation was 1:1, computer-generated in blocks of 4 and 6, stratified by centre, with allocation concealed in sealed web-based envelopes.</w:t></w:r></w:p><w:p><w:pPr><w:pStyle w:val="ListBullet"/></w:pPr><w:r><w:t>Inclusion: age 40–75 y, type 2 diabetes for ≥ 1 y, HbA1c 7.0–10.0 %, stable medication for 3 months</w:t></w:r></w:p><w:p><w:pPr><w:pStyle
